# File systems

Create file systems, and read, write, find and move the files in them. The calls start with `Vfs`, for virtual file system.

**Library:** [Maitento](index.md#maitento), for apps. More in [File systems](../../../concepts/file-systems.md).

| Call | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`VfsAppendLines`](#vfsappendlines) | Adds lines to the end of a file in a file system, creating the file if it isn't there yet. |
| [`VfsAppendText`](#vfsappendtext) | Adds text to the end of a file in a file system, creating the file if it isn't there yet. |
| [`VfsBatchEdit`](#vfsbatchedit) | Edits several text files in a file system in one call, each with its own list of operations. |
| [`VfsBatchRead`](#vfsbatchread) | Reads several text files from a file system in one call. |
| [`VfsCopy`](#vfscopy) | Copies a file or a directory to another path in the same file system. |
| [`VfsCreate`](#vfscreate) | Creates an empty file system in a namespace. |
| [`VfsDeleteDirectory`](#vfsdeletedirectory) | Deletes a directory from a file system. |
| [`VfsDeleteFile`](#vfsdeletefile) | Deletes a file from a file system. |
| [`VfsDestroy`](#vfsdestroy) | Deletes a file system and every file in it, permanently. |
| [`VfsEdit`](#vfsedit) | Edits a text file in a file system with a list of operations: find and replace, replace lines, insert lines or delete lines. |
| [`VfsExistsDirectory`](#vfsexistsdirectory) | Whether a directory exists at a path in a file system. |
| [`VfsExistsFile`](#vfsexistsfile) | Whether a file exists at a path in a file system. |
| [`VfsFind`](#vfsfind) | Searches a file system for files or directories by name, by content, or both. |
| [`VfsGet`](#vfsget) | Gets a file system's details by its name. |
| [`VfsListAll`](#vfslistall) | Lists the file systems in a namespace, or in the whole tenant. |
| [`VfsListDirectory`](#vfslistdirectory) | Lists what's directly in a directory of a file system: its files and directories, but not what's inside those. |
| [`VfsMkdir`](#vfsmkdir) | Creates a directory in a file system, with any parent directories it needs. |
| [`VfsMove`](#vfsmove) | Moves or renames a file or a directory within a file system. |
| [`VfsReadLines`](#vfsreadlines) | Reads a text file from a file system as a list of lines. |
| [`VfsReadText`](#vfsreadtext) | Reads a whole text file from a file system. |
| [`VfsTree`](#vfstree) | Lists a directory of a file system and everything below it, as a tree and as a flat list. |
| [`VfsWriteLines`](#vfswritelines) | Writes a list of lines to a file in a file system, replacing the file if it's there. |
| [`VfsWriteText`](#vfswritetext) | Writes text to a file in a file system, replacing the file if it's there. |

### VfsAppendLines

Adds lines to the end of a file in a file system, creating the file if it isn't there yet.

```c
jsonObject VfsAppendLines(string vfsName, string namespaceName, string path, jsonArray lines)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |
| `path` | `string` | The file's path, such as `/logs/today.md`. |
| `lines` | `jsonArray` | The lines to add, as a JSON array of strings. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The file after the write, as JSON: `$type` (`"file"`), `name`, `path` (the directory it's in), `size` in bytes, and `dateCreated` and `dateModified` (UTC).

The lines are joined with `\n`, with no line break added before the first or after the last. To add lines below a file's last line, start the array with an empty item: appending `["", "eggs"]` to a file that holds `milk` leaves `milk` and `eggs` on lines of their own.

Each item must be a JSON string: an item that is a number or `true`/`false` fails the call, and [`JsonArrayAdd`](json.md#jsonarrayadd) stores text such as `42` as a number.

The file's directory must already exist: unlike [`VfsWriteLines`](#vfswritelines), this call doesn't create it. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist. A write can be refused when the tenant is out of credit or has reached its storage limit.

### VfsAppendText

Adds text to the end of a file in a file system, creating the file if it isn't there yet.

```c
jsonObject VfsAppendText(string vfsName, string namespaceName, string path, string content)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |
| `path` | `string` | The file's path, such as `/logs/today.md`. |
| `content` | `string` | The text to add. Empty text adds nothing, but still creates the file. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The file after the write, as JSON: `$type` (`"file"`), `name`, `path` (the directory it's in), `size` in bytes, and `dateCreated` and `dateModified` (UTC).

The text goes on exactly as given: no line break is added before or after it, so include `\n` where you want one. Text is saved as UTF-8.

The file's directory must already exist: unlike [`VfsWriteText`](#vfswritetext), this call doesn't create it. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist. A write can be refused when the tenant is out of credit or has reached its storage limit.

### VfsBatchEdit

Edits several text files in a file system in one call, each with its own list of operations.

```c
jsonObject VfsBatchEdit(string vfsName, string namespaceName, jsonArray edits, bool atomic)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |
| `edits` | `jsonArray` | The edits, as a JSON array of objects such as `{"path": "/notes/a.md", "operations": [...]}`. |
| `atomic` | `bool`, can be empty | `true` to change nothing when any of the files is missing. Empty or `false`: each file is edited on its own. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: What happened, as JSON: `success` (`true` when every file was edited) and `fileResults`, one per file, each with `path`, `success`, `error` and `operationResults` (as [`VfsEdit`](#vfsedit) returns them). When `atomic` finds a missing file, `fileResults` holds only that file, with the error `File not found: <path>`.

Each item of `edits` is a JSON object with a `path` and `operations`, the operations [`VfsEdit`](#vfsedit) takes. Each file is edited as [`VfsEdit`](#vfsedit) edits one: its operations run in order, and if any of them fails, that file is left as it was. A file that can't be edited doesn't stop the others.

With `atomic` true, the call first checks that every file exists, and changes nothing if one doesn't. That check is all it adds: a file whose operations fail is still left as it was while the others are saved, so check `success` and each file's result.

Fails with `At least one edit is required` for an empty array, `Each edit must be a JSON object`, or `Each edit must have a path`. Within an edit, an operation that isn't a JSON object is skipped. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

### VfsBatchRead

Reads several text files from a file system in one call.

```c
jsonObject VfsBatchRead(string vfsName, string namespaceName, jsonArray paths, int maxLinesPerFile)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |
| `paths` | `jsonArray` | The files' paths, as a JSON array of strings. |
| `maxLinesPerFile` | `int`, can be empty | Read at most this many lines of each file. Empty or `0`: whole files. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The files, as JSON: `results`, one per path in the order given, each with `path` (as you gave it), `success`, `error` (`File not found` when there's no file there), `content`, `totalLines` (the file's line count, before any cut) and `truncated` (`true` when `maxLinesPerFile` cut it short).

A file that can't be read doesn't fail the call: its result says so. Each file's text is its lines joined with `\n`, so Windows line endings (`\r\n`) come back as `\n` and a line break at the very end is dropped; use [`VfsReadText`](#vfsreadtext) for a file exactly as stored.

Empty paths in the array are skipped, and an empty array fails with `At least one path is required`. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

### VfsCopy

Copies a file or a directory to another path in the same file system.

```c
jsonObject VfsCopy(string vfsName, string namespaceName, string sourcePath, string destinationPath)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |
| `sourcePath` | `string` | The path of the file or directory to copy. |
| `destinationPath` | `string` | The copy's full path, such as `/archive/report.md`: not the directory to put it in. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The copy, as JSON: `$type` (`"file"` or `"directory"`), `name`, `path` (the directory it's in), `dateCreated` and `dateModified`, and for a file `size` in bytes.

A file replaces any file already at `destinationPath`, but not a directory, and the directory that will hold the copy must already exist. A directory is copied with everything in it, to a path where nothing is yet; any missing parent directories are created.

Fails with `The file '<path>' does not exist` when nothing is at `sourcePath`, a missing directory included. Copying a file can be refused when the tenant is out of credit or has reached its storage limit. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

### VfsCreate

Creates an empty file system in a namespace.

```c
jsonObject VfsCreate(string name, string namespaceName)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The new file system's name, unique within the namespace. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace to create it in. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The new file system, as JSON, with the fields [`VfsGet`](#vfsget) returns.

The namespace must already exist (create it with [`NamespaceCreate`](namespaces.md#namespacecreate)), or the call fails with `Namespace '<name>' was not found.` A name already used in the namespace fails with `Failed to create VFS: VirtualFileSystem named <name> already exists in <namespace>`, and a tenant that has reached its plan's limit on file systems fails with `Failed to create VFS:` and the reason. Use [`VfsGet`](#vfsget) first when the file system may already be there.

### VfsDeleteDirectory

Deletes a directory from a file system.

```c
void VfsDeleteDirectory(string vfsName, string namespaceName, string path, bool recursive)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |
| `path` | `string` | The directory's path, such as `/old-reports`. |
| `recursive` | `bool`, can be empty | `true` to delete everything in the directory too. Empty or `false` refuses a directory that holds other directories. |

Pass `recursive` true to delete the directory and everything in it. Without it, only a directory that holds no other directories can be deleted, and it goes with the files directly in it. A directory that holds one with something in it fails with `The directory at <path> is not empty`, and one that holds only empty directories fails after its files have been deleted.

Don't delete `/`: that removes the file system's own root as well, and every later call on the file system fails until it is destroyed with [`VfsDestroy`](#vfsdestroy) and created again. To empty a file system, delete the files and directories in it.

A directory that isn't there fails the call. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

### VfsDeleteFile

Deletes a file from a file system.

```c
void VfsDeleteFile(string vfsName, string namespaceName, string path)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |
| `path` | `string` | The file's path, such as `/notes/old.md`. |

Fails with `The file '<path>' does not exist` when there's no file at the path. A directory at the path counts as no file: delete it with [`VfsDeleteDirectory`](#vfsdeletedirectory). Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

### VfsDestroy

Deletes a file system and every file in it, permanently.

```c
void VfsDestroy(string name, string namespaceName)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |

A file system mounted into a running sandbox or code pipeline run can't be destroyed until the run ends: the call fails with `Failed to destroy VFS: VirtualFileSystem is mounted and cannot be destroyed`. One that is already being destroyed fails with `Failed to destroy VFS: VirtualFileSystem is not active`. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

### VfsEdit

Edits a text file in a file system with a list of operations: find and replace, replace lines, insert lines or delete lines.

```c
jsonObject VfsEdit(string vfsName, string namespaceName, string path, jsonArray operations)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |
| `path` | `string` | The file's path, such as `/notes/shopping.md`. |
| `operations` | `jsonArray` | The operations, as a JSON array of objects. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: What happened, as JSON: `success` (`true` when every operation worked and the file was saved); `operationResults`, one per operation, each with `success`, `error` and `replacementCount` (the matches replaced, or the lines replaced, inserted or deleted); and `file`, the file after the edit as [`VfsWriteText`](#vfswritetext) returns it, or `null` when nothing was saved.

Each operation is a JSON object, and its `type` (in any case) says what it does:

`replace`, the default when `type` is left out, finds the text `find`, exactly and with case, and puts `replace` (empty when left out) in its place. Only the first match changes unless `replaceAll` is `true`. It fails when `find` isn't in the file.

`replaceLines` replaces lines `startLine` to `endLine`, inclusive, with `content`; empty `content` deletes them.

`insertAfter` inserts `content` after line `insertAfterLine`; `0` inserts it at the top.

`deleteLines` deletes the lines listed in `deleteLines`, an array of line numbers.

Lines are numbered from 1, and `content` can hold several lines separated by `\n`. Numbers must be JSON numbers, not text: build the operation from JSON text with [`StringToJsonObject`](conversion.md#stringtojsonobject), such as `{"type": "deleteLines", "deleteLines": [3]}`.

The operations run in order, and line numbers refer to the file as the operations before have left it. If any operation fails, the file isn't changed at all. Put `replace` operations before line operations: a `replace` that comes after a line operation works on the text as it was before that operation, and undoes it.

Fails with `The file '<path>' does not exist` when there's no file at the path. Fails with `At least one operation is required` for an empty array, and `Each operation must be a JSON object`. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

### VfsExistsDirectory

Whether a directory exists at a path in a file system.

```c
bool VfsExistsDirectory(string vfsName, string namespaceName, string path)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |
| `path` | `string` | The path to check, such as `/reports`. |

**Returns** `bool`: `true` when there's a directory at `path`.

A file at the path gives `false`. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

### VfsExistsFile

Whether a file exists at a path in a file system.

```c
bool VfsExistsFile(string vfsName, string namespaceName, string path)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |

| `path` | `string` | The path to check, such as `/reports/latest.md`. |

**Returns** `bool`: `true` when there's a file at `path`.

A directory at the path gives `false`. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

### VfsFind

Searches a file system for files or directories by name, by content, or both.

```c
jsonObject VfsFind(string vfsName, string namespaceName, string path, string pattern, string grep, string grepMode, bool ignoreCase, int contextLines, bool includePreview, int previewLines, int maxResults, int maxDepth, string type, bool includeHidden)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |
| `path` | `string`, can be empty | The directory to search from. Empty: `/`, the whole file system. |
| `pattern` | `string`, can be empty | A glob that an entry's full path must match, such as `**/*.md`. Empty: any name. |
| `grep` | `string`, can be empty | Text that a file must contain on one of its lines. Empty: no content search. |
| `grepMode` | `string`, can be empty | `"regex"` to read `grep` as a regular expression. Anything else, empty included: plain text. |
| `ignoreCase` | `bool`, can be empty | `true` to match `grep` ignoring case. Empty: `false`. |
| `contextLines` | `int`, can be empty | How many lines before and after each match to return with it. Empty: `0`. |
| `includePreview` | `bool`, can be empty | `true` to return the first lines of each file found. Empty: `false`. |
| `previewLines` | `int`, can be empty | How many lines a preview holds. Empty: 30. |
| `maxResults` | `int`, can be empty | The most entries to return. Empty: 100. |
| `maxDepth` | `int`, can be empty | How many directory levels below `path` to search: `0` for `path` alone. Empty or `-1`: no limit. |
| `type` | `string`, can be empty | What to find: `"file"`, `"directory"` or `"all"`, exactly. Any other value, empty included, finds nothing. |
| `includeHidden` | `bool`, can be empty | `true` to include names that start with `.`. Empty: `false`. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: What was found, as JSON: `results`, each with `path`, `type` (`"file"` or `"directory"`), `size`, `dateModified`, `grepMatches` (with `grep`: each matching line's `line` number and `content`, with the `before` and `after` lines) and `preview`; `totalFound`, every match, including any past `maxResults`; and `truncated`, `true` when `results` was cut short.

Every parameter after `namespaceName` narrows or shapes the search. Pass empty text for any you don't need, except `type`, which must be `"file"`, `"directory"` or `"all"`.

`pattern` is a glob matched, ignoring case, against each entry's full path, which starts with `/`: `*` matches within one directory, `**` across directories, `?` one character, `[abc]` one of a set and `{a,b}` either word. So `**/*.md` finds Markdown files anywhere, `/*.md` only at the root and `/notes/**/*.md` under `/notes`. A pattern without a leading `/` or `**`, such as `*.md`, matches nothing.

`grep` keeps only the files with a line that contains it: as plain text, or as a .NET regular expression when `grepMode` is `"regex"`. `ignoreCase` applies to `grep` only. Directories aren't searched by content, so with `type``"all"` every directory that matches `pattern` is returned.

The search starts at `path` and goes down through its directories: `maxDepth``0` looks only in `path` itself, `1` one level further, and so on. Names that start with `.` are skipped, and their directories not searched, unless `includeHidden` is `true`. A `path` that names a file checks just that file.

Fails when `path` doesn't exist. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

### VfsGet

Gets a file system's details by its name.

```c
jsonObject VfsGet(string name, string namespaceName)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The file system, as JSON: `id`, `name`, `namespaceId`, `status` (`Active`, or `Destroying` while it is being destroyed), `mounts` (the runs it is mounted into now, each with `type`, `CapsuleProcess` or `CodePipelineProcess`; `associatedId`, the run's id; `location` and `mountTime`), `dateCreated`, `dateUpdated`, `dateDestroyed`, `tenantId` and `userCreatedById`.

Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist. Use [`VfsListAll`](#vfslistall) to see which file systems there are.

### VfsListAll

Lists the file systems in a namespace, or in the whole tenant.

```c
jsonArray VfsListAll(string namespaceName)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `namespaceName` | `string`, can be empty | The namespace to list. Empty: every namespace. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: The file systems, as a JSON array, each as [`VfsGet`](#vfsget) returns it.

Fails with `Namespace '<name>' was not found.` when the namespace doesn't exist.

### VfsListDirectory

Lists what's directly in a directory of a file system: its files and directories, but not what's inside those.

```c
jsonArray VfsListDirectory(string vfsName, string namespaceName, string path)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |
| `path` | `string` | The directory's path; `/` for the root. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: The entries, as a JSON array, each with `$type` (`"file"` or `"directory"`), `name`, `path` (the directory listed), `dateCreated` and `dateModified`, and for a file `size` in bytes.

Directories come first, then files, and names that start with `.` are included. Use [`VfsTree`](#vfstree) for a whole tree and [`VfsFind`](#vfsfind) to search. Fails when the directory doesn't exist. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

### VfsMkdir

Creates a directory in a file system, with any parent directories it needs.

```c
jsonObject VfsMkdir(string vfsName, string namespaceName, string path)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |
| `path` | `string` | The directory's path, such as `/reports/2026`. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The directory, as JSON: `$type` (`"directory"`), `name`, `path` (the directory it's in), `dateCreated` and `dateModified`.

A directory that is already there is returned as it is, with no error. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

### VfsMove

Moves or renames a file or a directory within a file system.

```c
jsonObject VfsMove(string vfsName, string namespaceName, string sourcePath, string destinationPath)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |
| `sourcePath` | `string` | The path of the file or directory to move. |
| `destinationPath` | `string` | Its new full path, such as `/archive/old.md`: not the directory to put it in. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The file or directory in its new place, as JSON, with the fields [`VfsCopy`](#vfscopy) returns.

A file replaces any file already at `destinationPath`, but not a directory. A directory moves only to a path where nothing is yet. Either way, the directory that will hold it must already exist. Fails with `The file '<path>' does not exist` when nothing is at `sourcePath`. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

### VfsReadLines

Reads a text file from a file system as a list of lines.

```c
jsonArray VfsReadLines(string vfsName, string namespaceName, string path)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |
| `path` | `string` | The file's path, such as `/notes/shopping.md`. |

**Returns** `jsonArray`: The lines, as a JSON array of strings.

The file is split at each `\n`: a file that ends with a line break gives an empty last line, and the lines of a Windows file keep their `\r`. Fails with `The file '<path>' does not exist` when there's no file at the path. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

### VfsReadText

Reads a whole text file from a file system.

```c
string VfsReadText(string vfsName, string namespaceName, string path)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |
| `path` | `string` | The file's path, such as `/reports/latest.md`. |

**Returns** `string`: The file's text.

The file is read as UTF-8: bytes that aren't valid UTF-8 come back as the Unicode replacement character (U+FFFD). Fails with `The file '<path>' does not exist` when there's no file at the path. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

### VfsTree

Lists a directory of a file system and everything below it, as a tree and as a flat list.

```c
jsonObject VfsTree(string vfsName, string namespaceName, string path, int maxDepth, bool includeFiles, bool includeHidden, string pattern)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |
| `path` | `string`, can be empty | The directory to start from. Empty: `/`. |
| `maxDepth` | `int`, can be empty | How deep to go, counting `path` as 0. Empty or `-1`: all the way. |
| `includeFiles` | `bool`, can be empty | `false` for directories only. Empty: `true`. |
| `includeHidden` | `bool`, can be empty | `true` to include names that start with `.`. Empty: `false`. |
| `pattern` | `string`, can be empty | A glob that files must match, such as `**/*.md`. Empty: every file. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The tree, as JSON: `root`, nested nodes each with `name`, `path`, `type` (`"file"` or `"directory"`), `size` and `children`; `entries`, the same as a flat list, each with `path`, `type`, `depth` and `size`; and `fileCount` and `directoryCount`, which counts `path` itself.

The tree starts at `path`, at depth 0. With `maxDepth`, directories at that depth are listed without what's in them, so `1` gives just what's directly in `path`. `pattern`, a glob as [`VfsFind`](#vfsfind) takes it, filters files only: every directory is listed. Names that start with `.` are left out unless `includeHidden` is `true`. A `path` that names a file gives a tree of just that file.

Fails when `path` doesn't exist. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist.

### VfsWriteLines

Writes a list of lines to a file in a file system, replacing the file if it's there.

```c
jsonObject VfsWriteLines(string vfsName, string namespaceName, string path, jsonArray lines)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |
| `path` | `string` | The file's path, such as `/notes/shopping.md`. |
| `lines` | `jsonArray` | The lines, as a JSON array of strings. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The file after the write, as JSON: `$type` (`"file"`), `name`, `path` (the directory it's in), `size` in bytes, and `dateCreated` and `dateModified` (UTC).

The lines are joined with `\n`, with no line break after the last. Each item must be a JSON string: an item that is a number or `true`/`false` fails the call, and [`JsonArrayAdd`](json.md#jsonarrayadd) stores text such as `42` as a number.

Missing directories on the way are created. There's no locking: the last write wins. Fails with `Directory already exists at '<path>'` when the path is a directory. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist. A write can be refused when the tenant is out of credit or has reached its storage limit.

### VfsWriteText

Writes text to a file in a file system, replacing the file if it's there.

```c
jsonObject VfsWriteText(string vfsName, string namespaceName, string path, string content)
```

| Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `vfsName` | `string` | The file system's name. |
| `namespaceName` | `string` | The namespace the file system is in. |
| `path` | `string` | The file's path, such as `/reports/latest.md`. |
| `content` | `string` | The file's new text. Empty text leaves an empty file. |

**Returns** `jsonObject`: The file after the write, as JSON: `$type` (`"file"`), `name`, `path` (the directory it's in), `size` in bytes, and `dateCreated` and `dateModified` (UTC).

Missing directories on the way are created, and the text is saved as UTF-8. There's no locking: the last write wins. Fails with `Directory already exists at '<path>'` when the path is a directory. Paths are from the file system's root, such as `/notes/todo.md`; the leading `/` is optional, and `..` can't climb above the root. Fails with an error starting `VFS <name>@<namespace> not found` when the file system or its namespace doesn't exist. A write can be refused when the tenant is out of credit or has reached its storage limit.
